title: What Is an LTRO Anyway?
主要内容: The European Central Bank introduced long-term refinancing operations (LTROs) to address the euro zone debt crisis. These operations involved lending money at very low interest rates to euro zone banks, enabling them to purchase higher-yielding assets or lend more to businesses and consumers. Banks could use sovereign bonds as collateral for the loans, although Greece's bonds were no longer acceptable due to a downgrade by Standard & Poor’s. In December, the ECB launched three-year LTROs, extending the repayment period and leading to a much greater takeup than usual. Spanish and Italian banks used their holdings of sovereign bonds as collateral, helping reduce sovereign bond yields and supporting peripheral countries like Spain and Italy, where yields had fallen due to the use of sovereign bonds as collateral.
